title: Gilded silver plate showing a Sasanian king hunting (attributed Shapur I or II)
language_note: Museum catalogue record in English; object itself carries no inscription. No regional-language original text exists for this record — it is included as a multimodal/artefact anchor (Pillar 4) rather than a cross-lingual text pair.
date: 4th century CE (production); reign attribution disputed between Shapur I, r. 240–272, and Shapur II, r. 309–379
findspot: Said to have been found in Anatolia (Turkey)
original_text_excerpt: Gilded silver plate showing a king hunting; the king sits astride a galloping fallow deer, which he grasps by the antlers with his left hand while plunging a sword into its upper neck; the king is wearing a crown with pendant, presumably pearl-drop, earrings...
original_text_note: This is the British Museum's own catalogue description, used here as the 'original record' field since the object is a visual/archaeological artefact rather than a text.
notes: Sasanian royal silver plate imagery is a recurring genre compared against Roman decorated silverware in the scholarship (see British Museum curator's comments). Good candidate for Pillar 4 (vision/artefact intelligence) rather than Pillar 1 cross-lingual retrieval.
